message.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    For a domain
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>\Omega \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    and a small number
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>\mathfrak{T} > 0</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    , let
                  </jats:p>
                  <jats:p>
                    <jats:disp-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>\mathcal{E}_0(\Omega) = \lambda_1(\Omega) + \mathfrak{T} \operatorname{tor}(\Omega) = \inf_{u, w \in H^1_0(\Omega)\setminus \{0\}} \frac{\int |\nabla u|^2}{\int u^2} + \mathfrak{T} \!\int \frac{1}{2} |\nabla w|^2 - w</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:disp-formula>
                  </jats:p>
                  <jats:p>
                    be a modification of the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>\Omega</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    . It is well known that over all
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>\Omega</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    with a given volume, the only sets attaining the infimum of
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>\mathcal{E}_0</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    are balls
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>B_R</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    ; this is the Faber–Krahn inequality. The main result of this paper is that, if for all
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>\Omega</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    with the same volume and barycenter as
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>B_R</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    whose boundaries are parametrized as small
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>C^2</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    normal graphs over
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>\partial B_R</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    with bounded
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>C^2</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    norm
                  </jats:p>
                  <jats:p>
                    <jats:disp-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>\int |u_\Omega - u_{B_R}|^2 + |\Omega \triangle B_R|^2 \leq C [\mathcal{E}_0(\Omega) - \mathcal{E}_0(B_R)]</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:disp-formula>
                  </jats:p>
                  <jats:p>
                    (i.e., the Faber–Krahn inequality is
                    <jats:italic>linearly stable</jats:italic>
                    ), then the same is true for
                    <jats:italic>any</jats:italic>
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>\Omega</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    with the same volume and barycenter as
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>B_R</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    without any smoothness assumptions (i.e., it is
                    <jats:italic>nonlinearly stable</jats:italic>
                    ). Here
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>u_\Omega</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    stands for an
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>L^2</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    normalized first Dirichlet eigenfunction of
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>\Omega</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    . Related results are shown for Riemannian manifolds. The proof is based on a detailed analysis of some critical perturbations of Bernoulli-type free boundary problems. The topic of when linear stability is valid, as well as some applications, are considered in a companion paper.
                  </jats:p>
title: Linear stability implies nonlinear stability for Faber–Krahn-type inequalities
container-title: Interfaces and Free Boundaries, Mathematical Analysis, Computation and Applications
